title: Replication is asynchronous: an acknowledged write can vanish on failover
caption: The primary replies before the replica has the write. If the primary dies in that gap, the promoted replica never saw it.

messages.label: OK
messages.note: The client sees success in under a millisecond.

messages.label: replicate order:9
messages.note: Shipping the write to the replica happens afterwards.

messages.label: primary crashes
messages.note: If it dies before that message arrives…

messages.label: promoted to primary
messages.note: …the new primary has no order:9. The write the client was told succeeded is gone.

scenarios.name: Alternative: WAIT for a replica
scenarios.summary: WAIT blocks until N replicas have the write: the loss window shrinks to almost nothing, at the price of a replica round trip per write. It is still not a consensus protocol.

messages.label: replicate order:9
messages.note: The write ships to the replica as usual.

messages.label: WAIT 1 100
messages.note: Block until 1 replica acknowledges, or 100 ms pass.

messages.label: 1 (replicas that have it)
messages.note: Now a failover to that replica keeps order:9. If WAIT returns 0, the app knows the write is at risk.

scenarios.name: Read from a replica
scenarios.summary: Replicas lag, so a read sent to one right after a write can miss it. Read your own writes from the primary.

messages.label: GET cart:5
messages.note: The next read is load-balanced to the replica…

messages.label: 2 items (old)
messages.note: …which hasn't applied the write yet. Usually milliseconds of lag, seconds under load.

scenarios.name: Risk: split brain
scenarios.summary: A partition cuts the primary off; the majority promotes the replica while the old primary keeps accepting writes. Those writes are discarded when it rejoins.

messages.label: PING
messages.note: A network partition: the sentinels can't reach the primary.

messages.label: promote to primary
messages.note: A majority of sentinels agree and promote the replica.

messages.label: SET order:10 paid → OK
messages.note: An app on the primary's side of the partition keeps writing to it, and gets OK.

messages.label: rejoins as replica: writes dropped
messages.note: Mitigation: min-replicas-to-write makes an isolated primary refuse writes after a few seconds.
